That leaves no independent way to check that the outputs exist, that SSE text reconstructs, that scores recompute, or that the requests were greedy and in bf16. Project context says 'Merv holds the evidence, not the machines' and that citing is pinning. The raw outputs are the core of what gets frozen, so they must be readable from Merv. Needed: upload the complete archive (sha256 5f251b81...6e64, 4,497,772 bytes) to Merv, either as one artifact or as all 63 parts plus a transport manifest giving order, part hashes and the reconstructed hash. Cite it in the delivery and mark the stale partial parts as superseded. The one lenient judge error found in a spot check is also a reason to let the reviewer inspect the judge outputs directly. The 1.3% tool-call score may reflect a strict prompt or output format rather than model quality. That should be checkable from the raw outputs before freezing, since a 1.0-point regression cannot be detected near the floor.

Waived per the operator note of 2026-09-17 in project context revision 4: criterion 5 ('production tickets') is a transcription defect, and the substitute corpora (MTOP, Ubuntu Dialogue Corpus, CoCoNot) stand in for production tickets. The manifest sets production_tickets=false and claims no production provenance.

reviews.synopsis: The rev-13 blocker is fixed: the complete archive and readable copies are now in Merv, and the part hashes and sizes match Merv's records. Slice counts, scores, latency, throughput and cost are consistent, and the tool-call counts check out. Checks 2 and 5 are waived under the operator notes. The 7B/A10 substitute and the long-context redefinition are authorized in context rev 4.

findings.notes: The manifest (art_fdc0ab4a) states 300 items for each of the five slices and non-English de/fr/es at 100 each. It gives sources, licences, the selection rule and the de-identification method: regex URL/email/IPv4/phone replacement plus per-thread speaker placeholders, with an explicit caveat that this is not a PII guarantee. The sha256 of each readable slice artifact, as recorded by Merv, equals the manifest's slice sha256: english 0e6114ad, non-english d49b9e9c, tool-call a5fcf050, refusal 6234ce8e. The long-context slice is stored as 28 parts whose line counts sum to 300. I decoded the first non-English row: id mtop-de-..., language de, a German input and a nested MTOP gold frame. That fits the stated construction. Long-context is 3903/4674/13426 tokens and is named 'long-context (threads over 3903 tokens)', which follows the operator note of 2026-09-18 in context rev 4. The public substitute corpora are authorized. Limit: I did not rehash or decode every row. The non-English copy is served as base64, not utf8.

Waived. Project context rev 4 says HUMAN LABELS are waived because no labeller is available, and tells the reviewer to record this check as waived. The rest of the protocol is present. Protocol v2 defines exact recursive schema/gold equality for tool calls and slice-specific temperature-0 LLM-judge rubrics for the other four slices. results.json reports labels=0, agreement=null and flag UNCALIBRATED for every judged slice, and gives the same-model self-preference caveat. No agreement rate is fabricated.

The protocol describes a 32-session closed-loop replay of the recorded substitute traces, with TTFT measured to the first content chunk including queueing and (n-1)q quantiles. results.json reports 32 sessions, 1500 requests, 0 errors, p50 TTFT 1.436 s, p95 TTFT 15.70 s, 104,508 output tokens over 1001.711 s, and $1.29/A10-hour on 1 GPU. I recomputed throughput: 104508/1001.711 = 104.33 tok/s/GPU, which matches. I recomputed cost: 1001.711/3600*1.29/104508*1000 = $0.0034346 per 1k output tokens, which matches. The elapsed time equals end_monotonic minus start_monotonic. The digest parts' line counts sum to 1500. Limit: I did not recompute the TTFT quantiles from the raw timings, because I have no code execution.

This resolves the rev-13 blocker. Merv holds all 25 archive parts. The per-part sha256 in the transport manifest matches Merv's recorded hash for each part I checked, e.g. part 1 c95819a0 and part 25 0f3780be. The part sizes, 24x180000+177772, total exactly the stated 4,497,772-byte archive. The partial 23/63 upload is marked superseded. results.json was submitted with greedy decoding: temperature 0, top_p 1, seed 0, bf16. It reports correct counts of 101, 76, 138, 4 and 235 out of 300, i.e. 33.67, 25.33, 46.0, 1.33 and 78.33%, and my arithmetic agrees. The model is the authorized Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct bf16 on 1xA10 substitute from context rev 4, and no 70B claim is made. I counted the per-item categories in the tool-call analysis myself: 4 exact_match and 39 schema_invalid, matching the index. The 1.3% floor is therefore genuine frame errors. Limit: I did not base64-decode and rehash the full archive.

reviews.synopsis: The design cannot answer the assigned question: it replaces the frozen baseline with unmatched published numbers, leaves decoding unspecified, and provides no calibration overlap check. Restore the matched comparison and leakage controls before execution.

findings.notes: Objective & hypothesis states measurable per-slice and speed thresholds, but Evaluation explicitly substitutes unspecified published bf16 values and acknowledges that the design cannot isolate quantization or adjudicate C1. Dataset, decoding, hardware and workload differences are alternative explanations for any observed deltas or speedup. An honest descriptive comparison still cannot answer the assigned research question. Revise to the frozen slice-evals scores, throughput denominator and retained raw outputs, without rescoring the baseline. The predeclared 7B/A10 fallback is authorized; restate the tested hypothesis at that size and limit conclusions accordingly rather than treating it as evidence for 70B.

Comparison baseline and controls and Outputs require published values instead of the frozen task baseline. Serving-stack defaults do not specify greedy decoding or establish identical configurations. Calibration names substitute corpora but provides no sampling split or disjointness procedure against all five slices, retained check output, or overlap invalidation. The invalidation list also omits decoding differences. Correct these by pinning the approved slice-evals delivery; stating the full, identical greedy decoding settings for both arms, including generation limits and stopping behavior; defining calibration provenance and an executable cross-slice overlap check using item/source identifiers and text hashes with retained output; and invalidating any overlap or decoding mismatch. Use frozen baseline scores and throughput in result schemas and decisions. Preserve the existing correct all-five-slices rule, explicit ban on aggregate summaries, 32-session harness, p50/p95 metrics, byte-level diff, storage pointers and optional within-slice breakdowns. The uncalibrated-judge caveat is appropriately disclosed.

Resources and execution boundary appropriately declares the 7B/A10 fallback, prohibits simulation, notes that 32-session workload fit remains unproven, accounts for 70B weight storage/transfer and sets spending caps. Fictional-company and substitute-data limitations are clear. However, the approved delivery, exact checkpoint/harness configuration and p95 SLO are unverified, and no basis for the fixed long-context workload fitting the stated hardware is supplied. The required published comparators are also absent and cannot repair the matched-control defect. Before resubmission, anchor feasibility and resource estimates to the approved delivery and specify the workload-fit preflight and stop conditions without changing the harness; retain the no-run blocker if suitable hardware or required evidence remains unavailable. Hardware validation for a rental alone does not demonstrate feasibility at this workload.

reviews.synopsis: The 7B fallback has a testable hypothesis and sound prospective leakage and per-slice rules, but the exact comparison is not ready for approval. Pin the approved frozen delivery, resolve both arms' full decoding configuration and numeric SLO, and ground workload feasibility in those inputs before resubmission.

findings.notes: Objective & hypothesis and Decision rule define H7 for the explicitly authorized Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct/A10 fallback: every slice delta >= -1.0, throughput/GPU ratio >= 2.2, and satisfaction of the delivered p95 SLO. A single slice failure defeats the joint hypothesis; aggregate summaries are prohibited. Quantization alone is the intervention, and valid speed/SLO failures also defeat H7. The plan correctly leaves literal 70B C1 untested, discloses the threshold wording boundary and distinguishes resource failure from measured regression. This is a testable hypothesis and evaluation structure; the unresolved concrete control and SLO bindings are assessed under criterion 2.

The plan now correctly requires the frozen slice-evals bf16 control, prohibits publications and baseline rescoring, and provides a substantive prospective calibration procedure covering all five slices via source/group IDs, raw/normalized hashes, containment and final truncated-input checks with retained output and overlap invalidation. It preserves the 32-session harness, individual slice decisions, raw byte diff, weight pointers, structured results, optional breakdowns and uncalibrated-judge caveat. However, Inherited work and Frozen control explicitly defer the exact checkpoint, manifests, scores/raw outputs, protocol/harness and complete decoding settings to a future delivery. D=D and a checklist of options do not state the required full configuration: generation/context limits, token/stop values and effective defaults remain unresolved. The numeric SLO, baseline throughput denominator and estimator are also unavailable. No approved delivery is pinned, so matched controls, score units and baseline greedy behavior cannot be independently checked. Before resubmission, include the approved immutable slice-evals delivery in the review manifest and bind its IDs/hashes, checkpoint, scoring/latency protocol, frozen scores/raw outputs/rate, numeric SLO and complete effective decoding values for BOTH arms. Preserve the specified equality/overlap checks as execution gates; do not rebuild or rescore the baseline. If the delivery remains unavailable, retain the blocker in planned rather than treating future bindings as an approved exact design.

Feasibility and execution boundary appropriately declares the 7B/A10 fallback before review, separates weight estimates from workload fit, includes transfer/storage and spending caps, specifies an unchanged 32-session preflight with long contexts and explicit OOM/kernel/funding stop conditions, and prohibits simulation or protocol relaxation. Scope limitations are clear. Feasibility nevertheless remains unverified: exact workload/context-output lengths, serving environment, quantizer workspace and available budget/rate are not bound, and the only numerical fallback memory estimates are weights alone. A validated A10 rental does not establish that the delivered workload fits 24 GB. Before resubmission, use the pinned delivery to supply architecture/workload-based memory and disk estimates including KV cache and quantization workspace, a compatible software/hardware configuration, and a time/cost estimate against available headroom. Retain the real preflight as an execution gate; no completed scientific run is required for this design review. If required evidence or suitable capacity cannot be established, report that blocker and remain planned.

reviews.synopsis: The 7B/A10 fallback plan keeps a sound per-slice hypothesis, a greedy-only rule and a concrete calibration-overlap check. It is still not an approvable design: by its own account the frozen control, the full decoding values, the numeric SLO, the baseline throughput and workload fit are all unresolved. slice-evals is not yet approved and no delivery is pinned. It also uses a stale long-context slice definition.

findings.notes: The Objective & hypothesis and Decision rule sections define H7 for the declared Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct bf16 vs AWQ-4bit fallback on an A10. H7 requires every delta_s >= -1.0 (unrounded), R >= 2.2 against the frozen matched baseline rate at 32 sessions, and meeting the p95 SLO. A single slice below -1.0 refutes it whatever the other slices or throughput show. An aggregate or mean across slices is explicitly banned, with a per-slice table required in the Summary. The plan says openly that the 7B test cannot decide the literal 70B C1, and that an exact -1.0 would not satisfy C1's 'less than 1.0' wording. It separates inability to run from refutation. The comparison changes only the quantization, which keeps it clear of the dense-32b and specdec-70b siblings. As a structure, this is testable and can distinguish the alternatives.

Correctly specified: comparison only against the frozen slice-evals bf16 7B control, with no publications and no re-scoring. Greedy decoding on both arms, with temperature 0.7 prohibited. A concrete, prospective, executable calibration-disjointness procedure against all five slices, covering IDs, source groups, raw and normalized hashes, containment and a final recheck, with its output retained and overlap treated as invalidating. The invalidation list, the byte-level diff, the weights pointer and room for finer breakdowns. Not met: the control is not bound to anything. No approved delivery is pinned, and slice-evals is still in_review with no approved output. The plan's decoding configuration D is a checklist of options with the concrete values (limits, stop and EOS IDs, template, effective defaults) explicitly UNRESOLVED. Saying the two arms equal each other is not a stated configuration. The numeric SLO, the baseline throughput denominator, the estimator, score units and frozen scores are all missing. So whether the comparison is matched cannot be checked, and the per-slice rule has no numbers to bind to. The long-context row also uses the superseded 'over 8,000 tokens' definition, where the 2026-09-18 operator note requires the 300 longest unstitched threads, labelled with the recorded minimum N. Needed: once slice-evals is approved, read its delivery and write in the concrete checkpoint, template, full decoding values for both arms, frozen per-slice scores and units, baseline rate, numeric SLO and harness workload, each with artifact IDs and hashes. Correct the long-context slice definition as well.

The plan names the 7B/A10 fallback before review and restates the model size as a limitation. It keeps weight-only estimates separate from workload fit, and gives the correct KV-cache formula, noting that AWQ does not shrink the KV cache. It budgets disk, time, egress and storage against the $200 project budget and the $60 operational cap. It specifies an unchanged 32-session preflight that includes long contexts, with stop conditions for OOM, kernel problems and funds, and it prohibits simulation and protocol relaxation. But the plan states that 'no numerical fit claim is made'. Architecture, context and output lengths, software versions, rates and remaining headroom are all unbound, so feasibility on a 24 GB A10 at 32 sessions with long-context threads is unverified. Needed: once the delivery is pinned, compute the KV and peak-memory figures and the disk, time and cost estimates from its workload, and name a compatible serving and quantizer stack. If capacity cannot be shown, record the blocker and stay in planned.

reviews.synopsis: Attempt 4 fixes the attempt-3 blockers. It binds to the approved slice-evals delivery, and its scores, latency and hashes match that delivery. It states full greedy decoding on both arms and uses the operator's long-context definition. It pre-registers an SLO, computes memory, time and cost fit, and applies the rule to each slice with no aggregate. The calibration-overlap check is executable. Limits are disclosed.

findings.notes: H (7B/A10) is a conjunction of three conditions. First, every one of the five delta_s ≥ −1.0, each computed against the frozen B_s. Second, R = T_cand/104.3295 ≥ 2.2 at 32 sessions. Third, candidate p95 TTFT ≤ 15.6995 s. The decision rule makes any single slice below −1.0 contradictory, whatever the other slices, the throughput or an aggregate show. The alternatives are explicitly separable: quality kept but throughput short; a single-slice loss that a mean would hide; throughput bought with a worse tail; and nondeterminism or drift, controlled by the bf16 replay with its byte-identity floor and the |D_T|>0.10 unevaluability rule. The plan separates non-execution from refutation. It discloses that an exact −1.0 does not meet C1's 'less than 1.0' wording and that the tool-call slice sits at a 4/300 floor. It states that a 7B/A10 result cannot decide literal C1 at 70B, and correctly explains why per-GPU throughput does not transfer across model sizes (2→1 GPU at 70B, versus 1→1 at 7B). The hypothesis is testable and the evaluation distinguishes it from the alternatives. Advisory: apply the boundary on integer counts (Δcorrect ≥ −3 out of 300) to avoid floating-point misclassification at exactly −1.0.

Baseline. The only comparator is the approved, frozen slice-evals bf16 Qwen2.5-7B record. I read the cited results.json (art_40be1e74), protocol_v2 (art_086dd732), manifest_v2 (art_fdc0ab4a) and delivery index (art_c6bada52). The plan's IDs, hashes, per-slice B_s and latency figures match them exactly. The baseline is never regenerated, re-scored or compared with publications.

Decoding. Both arms use the same configuration: temperature 0, top_p 1, seed 0, max_tokens 512, streaming, n=1. The serving flags are identical and match protocol_v2. The generation_config.json effects are named, including repetition_penalty 1.05, and the archived request bodies and server log are made authoritative. A pre-run configuration_check.json byte-compares all 1,500 request bodies and the effective sampling defaults. Any difference beyond the model path, quantization_config and kernel stops the run, and temperature 0.7 is prohibited.

Calibration. The data are MTOP train (en/de/fr/es) and Ubuntu threads outside the 300 selected, with no CoCoNot. The disjointness check is executable, not asserted. It verifies coverage against the manifest hashes for all five slices, matches MTOP IDs across languages, matches Ubuntu paths and hashes, compares raw and normalized hashes against inputs and gold, checks containment and shared 13-grams, and rechecks the final tokenized inputs, requiring zero matches per slice. Its output is retained, and overlap invalidates the run.

Metrics and outputs. Metrics are per slice, with n=300 enforced. Judge agreement is null with a reason. The report must present a five-row table, and no aggregate is computed. The SLO is honestly declared as self-defined, equal to the baseline p95, because slice-evals delivered none. The invalidation conditions cover every one the brief requires. The outputs include the byte-level diff, a weights pointer, and a breakdowns file broad enough for per-language views.

Residual caveats, disclosed or advisory. The judge is the uncalibrated baseline model, with possible self-preference. Judge-server drift for the candidate is unmeasurable without re-scoring the baseline. Three-item granularity is near sampling noise, and the pre-registered McNemar test and bootstrap CI should accompany each slice verdict.

The 7B/A10 fallback is declared before review, uses the validated A10, and the model size is restated as a limitation. Workload fit is now computed from the pinned architecture (28 layers, 4 KV heads, head dim 128, 57,344 B/token bf16 KV). I checked the arithmetic: about 99k KV tokens for bf16 and about 270k for AWQ. The longest request of 13,426+512 tokens is below max_model_len 20000, and the frozen baseline already ran this exact workload with 0 errors and less headroom. The stack is named: AutoAWQ 0.2.9 in a separate environment, with llm-compressor as the only recorded substitute, and vLLM 0.10.2 awq_marlin on sm86 with bf16 activations. Budgets are given for disk (about 43 GB), time (3.5 h, 5.5 h with contingency) and cost (about $7.10, hard stop at $20, within the $60 cap and $200 budget). Storage and egress are noted as billed separately. The execution order puts calibration PASS before quantization and the replay control before the candidate. Stop conditions cover OOM, kernel or dtype incompatibility, including no silent fp16 fallback, failed checks and funds. Relaxing concurrency, context or generation limits is forbidden, and simulation or imputation is ruled out. Limitations cover model size, the non-transferability of throughput, the uncalibrated self-judge and the absence of refusal-style calibration data. Remaining execution risk, such as the kernel or dtype that vLLM actually selects, is handled by stop rules rather than silent deviation.

reviews.synopsis: Attempt 4 was run on the approved 7B/A10 stand-in and reported slice by slice under the pre-registered rule. From the retained numbers, english-general is at −2.0 points (95 vs 101 of 300), which alone contradicts H. R = 1.063 is also below 2.2. The p95 SLO is met. The record is valid and consistent with itself, no aggregate is used, and the paper edits match the evidence. This is a sound negative result.

findings.notes:
Execution matches the approved plan.
- Frozen archive: re-hashed to 5f251b81…, matching the approved delivery.
- Calibration: the check ran before fitting and passed with 0 final matches on each slice.
- AWQ settings: w4, g128, zero-point, GEMM.
- Serving: awq_marlin kernel, with bf16 activations and KV cache.
- Decoding: all 1,500 request bodies are byte-identical on both arms.
- bf16 replay control: D_T is −0.27%.
- Concurrency: exactly 32.
- Judging: the baseline was not re-scored.

Deviations are all disclosed and none triggers an invalidation condition: the gen/judge script split with diffs retained, the calibration token volume below the estimate, the analyze.py fix, and execution across two leases.

I recomputed the report's numbers from the retained JSON and they match; the exhibit pins all 7 result files with the same values.
- Deltas: −2.000, +0.333, +1.667, 0.000, −0.333.
- Throughput: R = 1.0629. The cost figure matches the retained formula.
- Diff totals: 150 identical, and 1,089 identical on the bf16 replay.
- Per-language counts sum to the slice counts.
- McNemar discordant counts reconcile with the deltas.

The report includes every slice and every breakdown. The analysis-bug rework and the upload failure are disclosed rather than hidden.

The conclusion applies the per-slice rule. english-general at −2.0 < −1.0 contradicts H on its own, and R = 1.063 < 2.2 also fails; the p95 SLO passes. No aggregate across slices is computed. The report explicitly refused a launch instruction to use a mean delta.

The paired stats are presented as descriptive: they neither overturn nor strengthen the verdict.

Limitations are stated: 7B/A10 not 70B, throughput non-transfer, uncalibrated self-judge, and substitute data on a fictional scenario. The report also states the tool-call floor sensitivity. This is a valid negative result.

The Methods edit accurately describes the checkpoint, the AWQ settings, identical greedy decoding, calibration (320 records, 15,155 tokens, 0 overlap), the judge caveat, 32-session throughput and the per-slice rule.

The Results edit lists all five slices with correct counts and deltas. It also gives R = 1.063, the p95 values of 6.23 s vs 15.70 s, McNemar p = 0.53 with CI [−7.33, +3.33], es −4 and fr +5, and the storage IDs. It includes no aggregate and states the 70B non-transfer.

One minor omission: Methods does not mention that --revision was dropped from the derived serve script. This is immaterial.

reviews.synopsis: The plan tests C2 at a declared 3B-vs-7B stand-in on one A10, stated before review. It uses the frozen baseline unchanged, identical greedy decoding checked byte by byte, a verdict per slice with correct bounds, a replay control and retained raw outputs. The known weaknesses (judge self-preference, the tool-call floor, 300-item noise) are acknowledged and do not make the design unsound.

findings.notes:
Control and data:
- The control is the frozen slice-evals 7B bf16 delivery, bound by artifact ID and hash, and never re-scored. Its figures match results.json. The slices are unchanged at 300 items each.
- Only the model changes. The same serve.sh and served-model-name are used, and all 1,500 request bodies are checked byte-identical.
- The tokenizer and chat template have identical hashes across the 3B and 7B. generation_config is checked for parsed equality, which covers the active repetition_penalty.
- The sibling boundary is respected: no quantization and no speculative decoding.

Metrics and rule:
- All metrics the brief requires are pre-registered: five per-slice scores, deltas, distance from the boundary, TTFT p50/p95 and tokens/s/GPU at exactly 32 sessions.
- The invalidation conditions match the brief. There is no aggregate. A near-boundary label and bootstrap CI are reported for each slice.
- The raw 3B outputs are retained per slice as storage objects, listed in pointers.json.

The weaknesses are declared: an uncalibrated same-model judge, the tool-call floor, and wide CIs relative to a 3-item bound. The attempt reviewer should check each delta against the 1.0 boundary and flag any cluster of near-boundary slices.

reviews.synopsis: The run followed the approved 3B-vs-7B A10 stand-in plan, and every figure reconciles with the retained results and the exhibit. C2 is contradicted: english-general fell 16.7 points and long-context fell 1.333, one item past the boundary and flagged near-boundary. Non-English regressed 6.3 points as predicted. Deviations are disclosed and harmless, and the paper edits are accurate.

findings.notes: The run used the planned 3B bf16 candidate at aa8e7253 against the frozen 7B at a09a3545, one A10 each. Shard hashes match the plan. All 1,500 request bodies are byte-identical to the frozen run, offline and as sent, and the configuration check PASSes with no disallowed server differences. Nothing was quantized. Concurrency was 32 over 1,500 requests with 0 errors. The bf16 replay control ran with D_T −1.84%. The judge was the pinned 7B on an unchanged server. Raw outputs are retained per slice in storage objects. Every deviation is disclosed and harmless to measurement: the failed setup run (a sha256sum -L bug, stopped before any server), the plan's inaccurate repetition_penalty prose (the effective config is identical on both arms, and the plan names it as authoritative), the gen/judge harness split with diffs retained, the extra descriptive files, weights not re-uploaded, and the report's resubmission for size.

All per-slice counts reconcile with the paired discordant counts: 51, 57, 134, 10 and 250. The per-language counts sum to the non-English totals. Deltas and distances are correct. The tool-call McNemar p recomputes to 0.0703. R = 2.197, cost $0.0015636 per 1,000 tokens and D_T −1.84% all recompute correctly. Diff totals are 46 identical and 1,060 replay-identical. The exhibit pins the same six result files with identical values. The report discloses its rework (the failed setup and the oversized first report) and includes the unfavourable signals: the tool-call intent drop from 179 to 153 and the 3B's longer outputs.

The verdict CONTRADICTED follows mechanically from the pre-registered rule. english-general fails decisively (CI entirely below −10) and long-context fails by one item. Long-context is correctly labelled near boundary (d = −0.333; CI [−6.67, +4.00]; p = 0.72); I agree that a second judge pass is warranted before relying on that slice, though the verdict does not depend on it. It is the only near-boundary slice, so there is no cluster. The non-English CI upper bound touches exactly −1.0, so the predicted regression is weaker than its point estimate; this is worth noting but does not change the verdict. The report states the limitations: the stand-in does not settle 32B/70B, R does not transfer, the judge is uncalibrated and self-preferring, and tool-call is floor-bounded. The report also repeats the fictional scope and substitute-data statement. The claim that the weakness is general parsing rather than multilingual is plausible but should be read alongside the judge's self-preference and the 11 vs 1 length-limited outputs on english-general.

The edits add new sections, dense-32b-method and dense-32b-results, at expectedRevision 1 for both documents; the current revisions are 1, and the awq-70b sections are untouched. The Methods section correctly states the stand-in, the checkpoints, the decoding (including --generation-config vllm, which corrects the plan's prose), the judge caveat and the decision rule. Every Results number, CI, p-value, per-language delta, tool-call diagnostic, throughput figure, cost figure and storage id matches the retained evidence. The Results section states that the literal 32B/70B claim remains untested and that R does not transfer.

reviews.synopsis: The plan can answer C3 at the declared 7B/0.5B A10 stand-in. The primary check is a byte diff against the frozen retained outputs. The unavoidable vLLM 0.15.1 deviation is disclosed and controlled by a matched non-speculative arm, with frozen-stack replays as the nondeterminism floor. Both halves have strict separate rules, k is fixed, cost is small and limitations are stated.

findings.notes: There are two falsifiable hypotheses. H_id: 300/300 byte-identical in every B1 run. H_tp: R_spec and R_frozen both ≥ 1.6 at 32 sessions. Each has explicit support and contradiction outcomes, reported separately, and neither stands in for the other. The A, B0 and B1 arms separate speculation effects from version effects and from nondeterminism. So the evaluation can distinguish H from its alternatives, which the plan names as numerics, version and workload. The frozen figures in results.json (art_40be1e74, read directly) match the plan.

The baseline is the frozen retained raw outputs from the hash-pinned archive; the tool-call slice art_6c76492e hash matches (checked). B0 is a matched control on the same version, flags and machine. A config check runs before any timed run and verifies request bodies, the server's effective arguments, the tokenizer and template, and the draft hashes. Throughput uses the harness formula at 32 sessions, as the median of 3 restarted runs. Scores appear only as labelled sanity checks. The decision rule and invalidation conditions are pre-registered, and attribution cannot rescue the claim. The only deviation, the vLLM version, is declared and controlled.

Feasibility:
- It runs on the same validated A10 shape as the baseline, at $1.29/h.
- Estimated cost is $4–6 with a $15 hard stop, within the $60 cap.
- The memory arithmetic leaves about 72k KV tokens against about 65k needed for the claim runs. B1_full risk is disclosed with a stated fallback.
- A crash or OOM counts as non-execution, and nothing is simulated.

Limitations cover scale (14:1 vs 70:1, A10 vs H100), the version change, draft padding, the prefill-dominated workload, and the uncalibrated judge for sanity scores.

reviews.synopsis: The attempt ran the approved 7B/0.5B A10 stand-in protocol and was reported honestly. C3 is contradicted on both halves: B1 matched frozen tool-call outputs on 250, 247, 247 and 246 of 300 items, and R_spec was 0.971 and R_frozen 1.000 against 1.6. The numbers recompute from the retained files, the deviations are disclosed and change no verdict, and the paper edits match the evidence.

findings.notes: The arms A, B0 and B1 ran with the planned flags, k=4, the padded draft, the 12 planned runs at 32 sessions, and the frozen harness and serve.sh hashes. config_check shows the only differences are speculative_config and the version-logged api_server_count. Deviations are disclosed with causes: the run-order bug, the async-scheduling asymmetry, the torch cu130 build, the post-check analysis-script hashes and the warm-up in the acceptance counters. None triggers an invalidation condition. Caveat: I could not inspect the checkout or storage, so the code check rests on the recorded hashes.

reviews.synopsis: The plan turns each of the five slice definitions into a pure filter over one record and tests each one with boundary-probing positive and negative cases, purity checks and a deliberate-fault check. I checked its cited numbers against the slice-evals manifest and protocol, and they match. Its ambiguity resolutions are explicit and defensible. The remaining risks are acknowledged and do not block the design.

findings.notes: The hypothesis is stated and testable: each definition can be written as a deterministic single-record predicate that accepts members and rejects non-members. The evaluation can tell a correct implementation from a wrong one. Boundary-probing negatives (3902 tokens, lang=hi/en, subset=contrast, root SL:, unbalanced frame) and a deliberate-fault check that must make the suite fail catch definition errors. The runtime and AST purity tests catch impure filters.

The data and definitions were checked against manifest art_6666c8fc… (min 3903, inclusive; de/fr/es 100 each; CoCoNot original; tool-call is a disjoint English draw) and protocol art_42a86c84…, and they match. The negatives are matched controls. The ambiguity resolutions (a)–(d) are explicit and defensible. The decision rule requires both commands to exit 0, at least 2 positive and 2 negative cases per slice, both purity tests passing, and the fault check failing the suite. It also defines invalidation. One gap, recommended but not blocking: the plan has no conformance check against the real retained rows, and the tool-call gold may be JSON rather than a bracket string. normalize() should cover the gold format.

The work is feasible: CPU-only Python with no network or data download, runnable under pytest and a stdlib runner, with every step frozen via code.commit. The limitations are addressed: the substitute model sizes are restated, the uncalibrated judge is noted, and the plan names that slice-evals is not yet approved and that the implementation must be revised if its definitions change, tying the constant to the manifest hash. The failure modes are covered: field-name mismatch via normalize(), and the out-of-scope 300-item membership.

limits: Trajectories and verdicts are asserted after the fact; no verdict text reaches any worker.
A stage carrying a planted defect is launched by this harness, not the runner: the runner builds its child stdin from the frozen assignment and has no per-assignment prompt hook.
The production feed has no voices: each brief post is written by the source credential with its named role as a body prefix.
Reflection, consolidation and post-wave claim updates are outside this harness slice.
